odia: ଦେଉଳ ତୋଳେଇଲେ ନାଁ ପଡ଼େ, ବାଟରେ ହଗିଲେ ନାଁ ପଡ଼େ
title: A name for what?
literal_meaning: Have a temple built and your name spreads; defecate on the road and your name spreads.
explanation: The same phrase, “your name spreads”, carries two very different kinds of attention. Building a temple supplies the respectable image; fouling the road abruptly drags it down into coarse comedy. The dictionary places the saying under notoriety, after a separate sense for good reputation. Being talked about is therefore not enough to tell whether someone is admired or condemned. In an editorial everyday use, the line can puncture a boast about publicity by asking what earned it. Its shock is part of the contrast, not an instruction to humiliate a person or a claim about a particular temple builder.
meaning_odia: ଦେଉଳ ତୋଳାଇଲେ ଲୋକେ ନାଁ କହନ୍ତି, ବାଟ ଅପରିଷ୍କାର କଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନାଁ କହନ୍ତି—କିନ୍ତୁ ଦୁଇଥର କହିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ସମ୍ମାନର ଚିତ୍ର ପଛକୁ ହଠାତ୍ ଏମିତି ଅଶୋଭନ କାମ ଆଣିବାରେ ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଝଟକା ଅଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ମଧ୍ୟ ସୁଖ୍ୟାତି ଓ ଅପଯଶକୁ ଅଲଗା ଅର୍ଥରେ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ କେତେ ଲୋକ ମୋ କଥା କହୁଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଗର୍ବ କରିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ କାହିଁକି କହୁଛନ୍ତି, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ। ନାଁ ହେବା ଓ ଭଲ ନାଁ ହେବାର ତଫାତକୁ ଏହି କଟାକ୍ଷ ମନେ ପକାଏ।
english_summary: Attention alone cannot distinguish an admired reputation from notoriety.
odia_summary: ନାଁ ହେବା ମାତ୍ରେ ସୁନାମ ହୁଏନାହିଁ; କେଉଁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ହେଲା, ସେଇଟି ଅସଲ କଥା।
usage_example: Original imagined example: After a noisy argument at a neighbourhood meeting, a participant boasts that everyone is talking about him. A friend quotes the saying and asks whether he wanted to be remembered for the quarrel or for helping solve the problem. No actual meeting or person is being described.
cultural_context: The coarse bodily verb is retained in the exact quotation and literal translation. The example uses a non-bodily modern situation. The Radhanath quotation in the preceding dictionary sense is a separate named literary example and is not presented as the author of this saying.
